item.title: US stocks give back some of the rally sparked by Trump's talk of negotiations with Iran
item.description: NEW YORK (AP) — With airstrikes still battering Iran and missiles still targeting sites across the Middle East, some of the optimism that sent stocks rallying the day before drained out of Wall Street on Tuesday. item.title: UPDATE: Normal police give update on condition of six shot Sunday morning
item.description: All six victims of the shooting in Normal, Illinois on March 22, 2026 are in stable condition and the Normal Police Department is still seeking the public's assistance with the investigation.

item.title: Fire out and shelter-in-place order is lifted after oil refinery explosion near Texas coast
item.description: An oil refinery fire near the Texas coast was put out Tuesday and a shelter-in-place order was lifted, hours after a large explosion at the complex shot plumes of smoke into the air, officials said. No one was injured in Monday's explosion at the Valero refinery in Port Arthur, about 90 miles (145 kilometers) east [...]

item.title: As national average nears $4, here's how close gas prices are to 2022 records
item.description: Every state saw record gas prices in 2022. Some are getting close to surpassing those milestones.

item.description: President Donald Trump has cast another mail ballot in Florida as he continues to publicly bash the voting method as a source of fraud and push Congress to curtail the practice. item.title: Illinois State Police complete Next Generation 911 upgrade
item.description: The Illinois State Police have completed upgrades to Next Generation 911 at 169 public safety answering points across the state, which will support geospaical call routing, text-to-911 capabilities, and potentially allow people to send photos and videos in the future.

item.title: Pizza Payaa wins big at International Pizza EXPO in Las Vegas
item.description: Pizza Payaa in Normal, IL won 2nd place for Best Detroit Style Pizza and Top Five for overall pan pizza at the International Pizza Expo in Las Vegas.

item.title: Series of Peoria County car thefts cause Sheriff's Office to issue warning
item.description: The Peoria County Sheriff's Office is warning residents to stay vigilant after a string of vehicle thefts and break-ins over the weekend, with suspects stealing vehicles with keys left inside and checking door handles for valuables.

item.title: Normal man released with conditions after arrest for allegedly recording his neighbor
item.description: A Normal man was released from jail pending his arraignment after he allegedly admitted to recording his neighbor without her knowledge, facing multiple charges including burglary and stalking.

item.title: Doctors Day celebrates healthcare professionals' dedication
item.description: Libby Tillman, a first-year Med Student at U of I College of Medicine Peoria, was inspired to pursue a career in medicine after witnessing her mother's battle with peripheral vascular disease, and is now dedicated to helping others deal with chronic illnesses.

item.title: Bloomington seeks long-term water supply for lakes
item.description: The City of Bloomington is seeking a long-term water supply for Lake Bloomington and Evergreen, with a project cost estimated to be between 80-100 million dollars and planning expected to take years.

item.title: ISU men ready for first trip to NIT Final Four, women advance to WNIT Fab Four

item.title: Dog rescued during Peoria house fire
item.description: The Peoria Fire Department responded to a house fire on Monday, displacing two people and causing an estimated $20,000 in damage, with the cause of the fire still under investigation.

item.title: Director of Wenona Food Pantry leads effort for the pantries new home
item.description: Sandy Naylor, director of the Wenona Food Pantry, has been working to secure a new building for the pantry for over a year, and with the help of the community, she is nearing her goal of providing the needed assistance to those in need.

item.title: Deadline approaching for Peoria neighborhood mini-grants application
item.description: The City of Peoria is offering neighborhood mini-grants to neighborhood associations and homeowner associations to use for improvement projects, with applications due soon and grants worth up to $5,000 for first-time applicants and up to $2,500 for returning applicants.
